text:
Aria: heads-up: I just saw a customer hit duplicate side-effects when our JS SDK retried a POST after a 429. No jitter and it ignored Retry-After. They used a payment endpoint so we need a clear DX and SDK change.

Tomas: can you paste the captured HTTP sequence? curious if Retry-After was present or not.

Aria: logs: 
```
-> POST /v1/payments
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
  Content-Type: application/json
<- 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 0
  X-Request-Id: rq_9ab
-> POST /v1/payments
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
  Content-Type: application/json
<- 201 Created
```
(no idempotency header present)

Priya: hmm Retry-After: 0 is bad signal; some infra emits that when queueing. Regardless, clients should not immediately retry POSTs without an idempotency key.

Marco: Agreed. Proposal for SDKs:
- Treat 429 specially: read Retry-After if present and use it as base delay (if > 0).
- Otherwise use exponential backoff with full jitter: base=120ms, factor=2, cap=8s. jitter=random_between(0, backoff).
- Default max retries = 4 for 429 and other 5xx transient errors.
- Never auto-retry POST/PUT/PATCH unless Idempotency header exists OR user opts into "unsafe_retries": true.

Tomas: For parity across languages we should pick the header name (X-Redwood-Idempotency) and behavior: SDKs may auto-generate a v4 UUID for write ops when auto-idempotency=enabled. But generation should be opt-in until we test.

Aria: From a DX perspective onboarding friction: many users don't know to set idempotency keys. Can we ship a short sample app that demonstrates payments-safe retry patterns and an opt-in toggle in the SDK? examples-bot: can you create an issue?

examples-bot: created examples/issue#213: "payments-safe-retries-sample" and assigned to @Marco. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/issues/213

Priya: server-side suggestions too: store idempotency records for N hours (24h default), and if a request arrives with an existing key while first is still processing, return 202 with an operation id. If duplicate after completion, return the recorded response (body + status). That prevents double-charges if the client replays.

Marco: Also add server telemetry for when Retry-After is 0 or missing so we can correlate with queued requests.

Tomas: Small doc checklist we can paste in CHANGELOG / SDK release notes: 
- 429 handling: respect Retry-After header when provided
- Default to exp backoff + full jitter (base=120ms, cap=8s, factor=2)
- max_retries = 4 for transient errors
- Do not auto-retry write requests without idempotency header unless user explicitly enables auto-idempotency
- Provide opt-in "auto_idempotency" with header X-Redwood-Idempotency, generated as UUIDv4 by SDK when enabled
- Surface retry metadata in logs (rw.retry_count, rw.retry_reason) and in HTTP header X-RW-Retry-Count
- Add sample app demonstrating safe retries and server pairing

Aria: For the sample app please include: cURL, Node, and Python examples showing how to set Idempotency headers, and how to configure the SDK flag. Also show how to detect and surface operation-id when 202 returned.

Priya: security note: if SDK auto-generates keys, they must be ephemeral and hard to guess. Do not reuse across distinct logical operations.

Marco: implementation plan for JS SDK PR:
- config: { auto_idempotency: false } default false for now
- when enabled: attach X-Redwood-Idempotency: uuidv4() for POST/PUT/PATCH unless user provided one
- retry engine: on 429 -> if Retry-After > 0 use that; else use jittered exp backoff; limit retries to 4
- do not retry on 4xx other than 429
- add telemetry event 'sdk.auto_idempotency_used'

Tomas: will mirror in Python and Go SDKs. Let's also add integration test that simulates server returning 429 then 201 to ensure duplicate side-effects are prevented when idempotency key present.

Aria: ok I'll file the internal doc PR and write the short changelog blurb. Marco, happy to help on the examples PR. Thanks folks :thumbsup:

examples-bot: assigned examples/PR#451 to Marco -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/451

infra-bot: linking internal infra ticket: INFRA-778 (queueing service emits Retry-After:0)

Priya: one more tiny UX idea: surface a warning in the SDK if a user sets max_retries > 0 for write ops without idempotency header. Could save a lot of support tickets.

Marco: love that. We'll add a one-line warning log (rw.warn) and an optional error thrown if strict mode is enabled.
